title: When the Cellar Burns
premise: Folklorist Mara Villalobos arrives in the frost-bound village of Hollowmere to record songs the locals refuse to sing twice, only to discover that every photograph from her late grandmother's house now shows an extra chair — and a man seated in it who grows clearer each night. The chair-man is one of the village founders, bound by an unfinished ritual that traded memory for protection, and he needs Mara to complete it before the first frost writes its final pattern and claims her too. As she uncovers how the founders corrupted their covenant of shared memory into a tool of control, Mara must choose between finishing the ritual as written or breaking it entirely, freeing the village at the cost of her own recollections of the found family she's built there. She breaks it — burning the cellar archive where stolen memories are stored — and wakes with gaps in her past but surrounded by villagers who choose to remember her anyway.
about_author: Sable Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing oral histories in remote mountain communities before turning to horror. They write about the things families keep in basements and the songs people only sing once.

chapters.title: The Chair That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Mara Villalobos arrives in Hollowmere to record its songs, staying in her late grandmother's house. Sorting old photographs, she finds every image now includes an extra wooden chair — and a blurred figure seated in it. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: unease disguised as scholarly curiosity; the reader feels the house watching back.

chapters.title: Songs Sung Once
chapters.summary: Mara interviews villagers who each sing a fragment of a founding hymn, then refuse to repeat it, going pale when asked why. Old Tam Vey warns her: 'The song remembers you back.' That night the chair-figure appears sharper in the photos. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: mounting dread as hospitality curdles into collective secrecy.

chapters.title: What the Frost Writes
chapters.summary: Frost patterns on the windows form legible script overnight — names, dates, a countdown. Mara realizes the pattern advances nightly toward some final design. The seated man in the photographs now has a face she half-recognizes from a founder's portrait. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the supernatural becomes personal and urgent.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the church basement archive, Mara finds the founders' ledger describing a ritual of 'pooled memory' meant to protect the village through famine winters. The final page is torn out. The seated man appears in a dream, mouthing words she can't hear. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: revelation laced with grief — good intentions gone wrong.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Open Arms
chapters.summary: The village warms to Mara startlingly fast — meals appear, repairs get made, children call her 'cousin.' She realizes they're absorbing her memories into the pool; she's becoming theirs. POV: Mara, with an interlude from innkeeper Dora Hale. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging, poisoned by consent she never gave.

chapters.title: Dora's Confession
chapters.summary: Dora admits the ritual was perverted generations ago: elders harvest memories from outsiders and dissenters, storing them in jars in the cellar to extend their own lives. The torn ledger page named the price. The seated man was the last founder who resisted. POV: Dora. Emotional beat: guilt, complicity, and the first crack in the village's unity.

chapters.title: The Man in the Middle
chapters.summary: Through a blood-and-hymn rite, Mara pulls the seated man fully into the world: Edric Vale, founder, imprisoned in the pooled memory for trying to end the covenant. He tells her the ritual can be finished as written — sealing the village forever — or broken by burning the cellar archive. POV: alternating Mara/Edric. Emotional beat: alliance forged between two prisoners of different cages.

chapters.title: Counted Doors, Locked Lights
chapters.summary: The elders discover Mara's purpose and seal the village: doors won't stay open, lights die room by room, and the frost script reaches its penultimate line. Villagers Mara loves turn glassy-eyed, singing the hymn in unison outside her window. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: isolation at its peak; found family weaponized against her.

chapters.title: When the Cellar Burns
chapters.summary: On the final frost night, Mara and Edric descend into the cellar of jarred memories. The elders confront them; Dora turns against her own kind to hold the door. Mara ignites the archive — memories scream free, returning to their owners mid-scream — while Edric unravels the ritual's final knot with his last strength. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: cathartic, terrible climax; salvation that costs something real.

chapters.title: What We Choose to Remember
chapters.summary: Spring comes early. The village wakes with returned memories and gaps where the pool once held them; Mara has lost chunks of her past, including pieces of her bond with Dora and Edric, who faded with the ritual. But the villagers, remembering freely for the first time, choose to keep her. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — family rebuilt not by magic but by choice.
